title: Classify transient provider failures (529 overloaded, 5xx, network) as unavailable, not quota
observation: adapters/base.classify_failure matched 'overloaded' in QUOTA_PATTERN, so one transient Anthropic 529 surfaced by the Claude CLI wrote a one-hour machine-wide cooldown (DEFAULT_QUOTA_COOLDOWN) shared by every run, delegate and eval. 5xx, stream-disconnect and connection errors fell to process_error, which the provider breaker never counts. HTTPAPIAdapter already maps 5xx/529 to unavailable. Baseline on a 26-case labeled corpus: 0/12 transient cases correct, 3 false quota cooldowns (180 min). Root cause: one regex conflated capacity overload with budget exhaustion, and CLI workers had no transient class.
suggested_direction: Add TRANSIENT_PATTERN -> 'unavailable' after quota and invalid_model checks; drop 'overloaded' from QUOTA_PATTERN; pin with a labeled corpus and adapter-level tests.
acceptance: corpus: every case gets its label
single overload leaves the provider usable machine-wide; repeated overloads open the breaker
full suite no new failures vs baseline
risks: prose containing 'overloaded' in a Claude is_error result would still classify as a provider failure (now unavailable instead of quota, strictly less costly)
